title: Tuesday Daily Practice
subtitle: Reading test: polar bears (TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN and summary)
theme: P2 · Reading practice (paraphrase of a Cambridge passage)
source: Cambridge IELTS 16, Test 1, Reading Passage 1, viết lại cho lớp 4.0–5.0
intro: Làm lần lượt 4 bước, khoảng 55 phút. Làm trong 35 phút đầu như đi thi: không tra từ điển, không xem lại đáp án. Phần còn lại ghi sổ lỗi và nói tóm tắt. Hạn nộp 23:30 cùng ngày: đủ và đúng hạn được 20 Meow, muộn hoặc làm một nửa được 10 Meow.
send_today: Hoàn thành 4 bước trên web. Voice note ở bước 4 được gửi tự động khi bấm Nộp bài.

steps.title: Step 1 · TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN (câu 1–7)
steps.instructions: Đọc đoạn văn 1 lần, rồi làm 7 câu. Chọn A = TRUE, B = FALSE, C = NOT GIVEN. Không tra từ điển. Làm trong 20 phút như đi thi.

items.q: 1. Polar bears have many health problems because of the fat under their skin.
items.explain: Bài nói gấu có lớp mỡ nhưng không bị các vấn đề đó (Yet polar bears do not seem to suffer).

items.q: 2. The study by Liu and his colleagues compared different groups of polar bears.
items.explain: Nghiên cứu so sánh gấu Bắc Cực với gấu nâu, không so sánh các nhóm gấu Bắc Cực với nhau.

items.q: 3. Liu's team was the first to compare the genes of polar bears and brown bears.
items.explain: Bài không nói nhóm này là người đầu tiên.

items.q: 4. Polar bears can lower their bad cholesterol through their genes.
items.explain: Gen APoB làm giảm LDL, loại cholesterol xấu.

items.q: 5. Female polar bears can go for about six months without eating.
items.explain: Gấu cái nhịn ăn khoảng sáu tháng (For about six months they fast).

items.q: 6. The bones of female polar bears are very weak when they leave the den in spring.
items.explain: Even so, their bones remain strong and dense.

items.q: 7. The way polar bears keep their bones dense might one day help people.
items.explain: Kiến thức này có thể giúp người nằm liệt giường và phi hành gia.

steps.passage:
Polar bears are facing more and more threats from climate change. If they disappeared, the effects could be serious. They are well adapted to the Arctic, where temperatures can fall to minus 40 degrees Celsius. One reason is that they have a layer of fat up to 11 centimetres thick under their skin. For humans, this much fat would lead to obesity and would raise the risk of diabetes and heart disease. Yet polar bears do not seem to suffer from these problems.

A study in 2014 by Shi Ping Liu and his colleagues may help explain this. The team compared the genes of polar bears with those of brown bears, their closest relatives, which live in warmer places. This helped them find the genes that let polar bears survive in one of the harshest places on Earth. They found that polar bears have a gene called APoB. This gene lowers the level of LDL, a type of bad cholesterol. In humans, changes in this gene are linked to a higher risk of heart disease. So studying polar bears may help scientists understand heart disease in people.

Polar bear genes may also help with osteoporosis, a disease that makes bones less dense. It is often caused by too little exercise, too little calcium or not enough food. Bone is constantly rebuilt: it is added or removed depending on how much nutrition is available and how much stress it takes. Pregnant female polar bears face extreme conditions. In autumn they dig dens in the snow and stay there all winter, both before and after their cubs are born. For about six months they fast. They must keep themselves and their cubs alive, using up their own calcium and energy. Even so, their bones remain strong and dense.

In 2008, the physiologists Alanda Lennox and Allen Goodship found an explanation for this. They saw that pregnant bears increased the density of their bones before they started to build their dens. Six months later, when the bears came out of the den with their cubs, there was no sign of major bone loss. Brown bears that hibernate cannot do this, so they must rebuild their bones the following spring. If scientists understand how polar bears remodel their bones, this knowledge could help bedridden people and astronauts.

Polar bears may also be important for other reasons. Their intelligence is mostly shown through anecdotes, but the stories are interesting. At Tennoji Zoo in Osaka, a male bear called GoGo used a tree branch several times to pull down a piece of meat that was out of his reach. Wild polar bears have also shown problem-solving skills, though less clearly than GoGo. In a study by Alison Ames in 2008, bears deliberately pushed objects into piles and then knocked them over, which looked like play. Such behaviour suggests that bears are more creative than we once thought.

Bears also seem to show emotions. Many bears have been seen hitting out at ice and snow when they have just missed a kill, which looks like frustration. Polar bears can also form unusual bonds with other animals. For example, a polar bear raised by hand called Agee has a close relationship with its owner, Mark Dumas, and they even swim together. This is surprising, because polar bears are known to hunt humans in the wild.

If climate change led to their extinction, we would lose possible medical discoveries. More importantly, we would lose an intelligent and majestic animal.

steps.title: Step 2 · Summary completion (câu 8–13)
steps.instructions: Điền một từ trong bài. Không viết quá một từ. Đọc lại đoạn văn ở bước 1 nếu cần.

items.label: 8. People think bears are not intelligent and can be ______.
9. In Tennoji Zoo, a bear used a branch as a ______ to reach a piece of meat.
10. The bear pulled down a piece of ______ that was out of its reach.
11. A wild polar bear worked out how to reach a platform where a ______ was standing.
12. Moving objects on purpose looks like a ______.
13. Bears hit the ice and snow when they miss a kill, which suggests ______.

steps.title: Step 3 · Error log
steps.instructions: Với mỗi câu sai ở bước 1 và 2, ghi số câu, dạng bài (True/False/Not Given hoặc summary) và lý do: không hiểu từ · bẫy số · Not Given nhầm False · viết sai từ · hết giờ. Cuối cùng viết: Next time I will ...

open.model: Q5: TRUE. I chose NOT GIVEN because I did not notice the word fast. Next time I will check synonyms before I choose NOT GIVEN.

steps.title: Step 4 · Speaking: summarise
steps.instructions: Ghi âm 30 giây: tóm tắt bài bằng 3 câu bằng lời của em, không đọc lại bài. Nói rõ một lý do vì sao cần bảo vệ gấu Bắc Cực.
lines: Tóm tắt bài polar bears bằng 3 câu.
steps.note: Thầy nghe cách em diễn đạt bằng từ khác và âm cuối.
